This stall reason is high in cases of extreme utilization of the MIO pipelines, which include special math instructions, dynamic branches, as well as shared memory instructions. When caused by shared memory accesses, trying to use fewer but wider loads can reduce pipeline pressure. Highly scattered memory accesses can also fill this queue when each access expands into many internal operations; improve access locality when this is the cause. This stall type represents about 57.7% of the total average of 36.7 cycles between issuing two instructions.
